title: ioctl_init: inbuf not consumed or cleared when INIT called after write on UNSET fd
description: When a userspace caller writes key bytes to an UNSET fd (for KEY_IMPORT) and then calls CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_INIT instead (perhaps by mistake, or as a deliberate state confusion attempt), the inbuf is NOT cleared by ioctl_init(). The fd transitions to OPERATION state with inbuf still allocated and containing key material. The key material sits in inbuf until close() is called (which calls inbuf_clear in the release handler). During the session lifetime, inbuf holds the (now-unused) key bytes alongside the active session state. This is not a use-after-free or functional bug (inbuf is unused by OPERATION fd), but it violates the FIPS 140-3 requirement that key material be zeroized as soon as it is no longer needed. The key bytes from the abandoned KEY_IMPORT write remain in kernel memory for the duration of the OPERATION session. Trigger: write(key_bytes) on UNSET fd → call INIT instead of KEY_IMPORT → inbuf holds key_bytes until close() → violates FIPS 140-3 'minimum time' key material retention requirement.
